edges.description: A choriocarcinoma component differentiates and its syncytiotrophoblasts secrete beta-hCG.
The combined components form an invasive, often rapidly growing tumor mass with metastatic potential.
beta-hCG stimulates estrogen production, which can cause gynecomastia.
Invasive growth of a testicular primary presents as a testicular mass.
Invasive growth of a primary mediastinal tumor, or mediastinal nodal metastasis, forms a mediastinal mass.
Rapidly proliferating mixed germ cell components in the ovary form a large unilateral adnexal mass.
Rapid pelvic/retroperitoneal mass expansion, capsular distension, or torsion causes acute or subacute abdominal pain.
Anterior mediastinal mass effect or pulmonary metastasis impairs respiration and causes dyspnea.
Platinum resistance permits persistence or relapse of the tumor mass.

nodes.description: The defining event of a mixed germ cell tumor is simultaneous (divergent) differentiation of the pluripotent transformed precursor along multiple embryonic and extraembryonic lineages, producing two or more coexisting histologic components: embryonal carcinoma (pluripotent), yolk sac tumor (extraembryonic endoderm), choriocarcinoma (trophoblast), teratoma (somatic tri-lineage), and seminoma/dysgerminoma (gonocytic). The specific combination determines the serum marker profile and biologic behavior.

nodes.description: Prenatal exposure to endocrine-disrupting chemicals is hypothesised to raise testicular germ cell tumor risk under the testicular dysgenesis syndrome model, but the evidence separates sharply by agent and should not be stated as one claim. For diethylstilbestrol, a meta-analysis of six studies estimates roughly a threefold increase in risk after in utero exposure. For organochlorine pesticides and polychlorinated biphenyls, the strongest available design, a nested case-control study measuring these chemicals directly in maternal serum biobanked during pregnancy, found no association.

evidence.snippet: By meta-analysis of data from the six qualifying studies, the summary odds ratio estimate of the in utero DES-testicular cancer association was 2.98 (95% confidence interval = 1.15 to 7.67).

nodes.description: Isochromosome 12p [i(12p)] is the hallmark cytogenetic abnormality of invasive post-pubertal-type germ cell tumors, present in the large majority of cases, and marks the transition from in situ GCNIS to invasive disease. nodes.description: KIT and K-RAS are the most significantly mutated somatic genes in germ cell tumors. KIT (a stem-cell growth factor receptor controlling germ cell survival, proliferation, and migration in normal development) is mutated in 18-25% of cases, chiefly in seminomatous components, and KRAS shows copy-number gain in the majority of tumors with activating mutations in roughly a quarter. The resulting KIT-RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK cascade is constitutively activated and drives proliferation of the transformed precursor.
